documents.unit: University of Colorado system (Office of Policy and Efficiency), applies to CU Boulder
documents.title: APS 6012 - Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.summary: A University of Colorado system policy, effective August 2026, covering responsible AI use in academic, research and administrative work. It mainly sets data, IP, procurement, disclosure and governance rules, and states that it "does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework", leaving that to faculty and units.
documents.stance_why: The document says "this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework" and lets schools, colleges, departments or programs set their own guidance, so it takes no coursework stance itself and delegates.

units.why: The brief description states the university is "committed to supporting the responsible exploration" of AI and "encouraging and supporting innovation". It is an institution-level statement of purpose and principles, so P56 fits; it is not a rule for coursework.
units.resolution_why: Coder A made the actor admin, coder B all. The sentence is the University's own statement of commitment ('The University of Colorado ... is committed to supporting the responsible exploration'), so it is addressed from the institution, not to all users; actor admin.
units.anchor: committed to supporting the responsible exploration of the rapidly growing field of AI tools
units.frag_end: in alignment with its mission and values.

units.why: The "Reason for Policy" says the policy "establishes a basic framework for the responsible, ethical, and secure use of AI". This states purpose and scope at institution level (P56).
units.anchor: establishes a basic framework for the responsible, ethical, and secure use of AI

units.why: The definition "Generative AI (GenAI) is a subset of Artificial Intelligence" fixes what the policy covers, so it is a definition (P61, informs).
units.anchor: Generative AI (GenAI) is a subset of Artificial Intelligence (AI) that can generate text,

units.why: The policy quotes Regent Law and says "This principal responsibility includes decisions about the use of AI tools", placing pedagogy-related AI decisions with faculty. That is who decides (P04), not an AI stance.
units.anchor: This principal responsibility includes decisions about the use of AI tools within those contexts
units.policy: Faculty have principal responsibility for decisions about the use of AI tools in pedagogy, curriculum, research and scholarly work, consistent with other Regent Laws and Policies.
units.fit_note: Responsibility is placed on tenured and tenure-track faculty with other faculty participating, citing Regent Law 5.A.1.B, not on each instructor individually. / Decision rests with tenured and tenure-track faculty collectively through governance, not necessarily the individual instructor.

units.why: "final decision-making authority on the use of AI at CU rests with the President and the Chancellors" names who holds authority outside Regent Law 5 contexts, which is P80 (who owns the policy).
units.anchor: final decision-making authority on the use of AI at CU rests with the President

units.why: "must comply with CU's data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies" binds any AI use for University activities to existing policies (P77, must).
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance restrict, coder B neutral. The sentence says use 'must comply with CU's data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies'. It points to other policies and does not itself limit which AI use is allowed, so neutral.
units.anchor: must comply with CU’s data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies
units.frag_start: The use of any AI tool
units.policy: Use of any AI tool, stand-alone or embedded, for University academic, research, scholarly and creative work or administrative activities must comply with CU's data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies.

units.why: "Users need to consider the security, privacy and handling of any information they provide to GenAI tools" tells users to protect what they enter, which is P50.
units.anchor: Users need to consider the security, privacy and handling of any information they provide

units.why: The same sentence adds users must evaluate "the quality and accuracy of the output", a verify-the-output rule (P31); the privacy half of the sentence is coded separately as P50.
units.anchor: evaluating the quality and accuracy of the output of the system
units.policy: Users evaluate the quality and accuracy of the output of the GenAI system.

units.why: "AI should be used in ways that preserve academic freedom, safeguard privacy and institutional data, maintain appropriate security and risk management, promote fairness and inclusion" lists principles that frame all AI use, so P56 (institution-level principles).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. The source sentence lists principles for AI use (academic freedom, privacy, security, fairness); the equity clause in the same sentence is coded separately. It is a real principle statement, so kept as P56. Topics changed from policy-evolution to privacy-data and governance because the sentence is not about review.
units.anchor: AI should be used in ways that preserve academic freedom, safeguard privacy and institutional data

units.why: "supporting ... appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities" is an equity aim in the ethical principles. P51 is nearest though it is a principle, not a no-paid-tools rule.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance neutral, coder B encourage. The passage says AI should be used in ways that 'support appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities', which favours access to AI; encourage.
units.anchor: support appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities
units.fit_note: States equitable access as a principle only; it says nothing about paid tools, alternatives or accommodations. / A principle of equitable access, with no statement about cost or alternatives.

units.why: "AI should not be used to deceive, manipulate, misrepresent, circumvent established requirements" is a general conduct ban on deceptive use, and the passage extends to "the integrity of ... teaching, or other academic work" (P74).
units.anchor: AI should not be used to deceive, manipulate, misrepresent, circumvent established requirements or controls

units.why: "individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI" lets units (and individuals) opt out of AI for particular activities and set alternative processes. P85 (units set their own rules) fits the named units; the individual element and the alternative-process clause are in the fit note.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P85, coder B P04. The passage names 'individuals and units', not instructors or assignments. P04 is the instructor/assignment-level type and P85 is the unit-level type; the sentence lists units first and is not about a per-assignment rule, so P85 with a fit note for the individual element. Actor kept as all, phase before-course (both coders agree). B's normalized policy is kept because it stays within the sentence. Dropped-type coder note kept: Covers units and individuals deciding certain activities go without AI and setting alternative processes, not specifically instructors choosing a course rule.
units.anchor: individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI
units.policy: Individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI and may establish appropriate alternative processes where feasible.
units.fit_note: Applies to individuals as well as units, and also allows alternative processes where feasible.

units.why: "AI should be used in ways that maintain and prioritize human judgment and creativity" is one of the policy's principles for all AI use at the University, so P56 (institution-level principles).
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit; it assigned P32 with a fit note that it is addressed to all users and to research and service as well as learning. The source sentence is a university-wide principle, and P32 is for students staying the primary problem-solver, so P56. The sentence is real policy text, so kept. B's fit note is recorded here. Dropped-type coder note kept: Addressed to all users and to research and service as well as learning; not specific to students.
units.anchor: maintain and prioritize human judgment and creativity

units.why: "Responsibility and accountability for decisions and outcomes cannot be delegated to an AI system" keeps humans accountable for decisions. P73 is nearest, but the sentence is general, not limited to decisions about individuals.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded unit_stance restrict, coder B prohibit. The sentence does not ban AI use; it bars handing responsibility for decisions and outcomes to an AI system, a limit on one way of using AI, so restrict.
units.anchor: Responsibility and accountability for decisions and outcomes cannot be delegated to an AI system
units.fit_note: Covers decisions and outcomes in general, not only consequential decisions about individuals. / General rule that accountability for any decision or outcome stays with humans; P73 covers decisions about individuals specifically.

units.why: "Users must recognize that AI systems may reflect or amplify inaccuracies, biases, or incomplete information and should exercise judgment" warns that output can be wrong or biased and asks for critical judgment (P31).
units.anchor: AI systems may reflect or amplify inaccuracies, biases, or incomplete information

units.why: "Oversight requirements will be defined through campus AI governance processes" says where oversight rules will come from, a question of who owns the policy, P80.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. 'Oversight requirements will be defined through campus AI governance processes' says who will set oversight rules, a real statement of ownership, so kept as P80. Topic changed to governance.
units.anchor: Oversight requirements will be defined through campus AI governance processes

units.why: "should not rely on AI as a substitute for qualified professional or institutional support services" directs people to human support in sensitive personal matters (P72); it concerns wellbeing, not coursework.
units.anchor: should not rely on AI as a substitute for qualified professional or institutional support services
units.fit_note: About sensitive personal, emotional or psychological matters and wellbeing, not about course help. / About emotional and psychological matters, not academic help.

P61.

units.anchor: may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses

This sentence says prompts, outputs and logs 'may be subject to disclosure upon request' under the Colorado Open Records Act, which is a public-records fact that P50 does not say. Constant comparison with P50's definition fails, so UNCOVERED (A's note kept; B's fit note is recorded here: public-records disclosure of prompts and outputs rather than vendor storage). Dropped-type coder note kept: Public-records disclosure of prompts and outputs rather than vendor storage.
units.anchor: Prompts, outputs, and related records (including logs, where applicable) may be subject to disclosure upon
units.uncovered_note: AI prompts, outputs and logs may be public records that can be requested under the Colorado Open Records Act.

documents.summary: A draft (12/23/24) from the Boulder Faculty Assembly and Center for Teaching and Learning that gives instructors four levels of AI use and sample syllabus language. It also advises on discussing rules with students, avoiding detectors, and citing AI use.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Security Guidelines
documents.summary: A CU Boulder Office of Information Technology page of data-security guidelines for generative AI. It limits AI tool use to Public data, points to campus-recommended tools, and asks users to verify output and vendor terms. It says nothing about coursework.
documents.stance_why: The page is about data security and says "AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public" and to "Use AI tools available and recommended", so it permits AI use under data conditions and sets no coursework rule. Coder A chose delegates because the page has no coursework stance; the nearest value that describes what the page does say is permit, since it allows AI use under data-classification conditions.
